svg.text: The keyhole standoff behind the corner tile's slot, from the front and from the side, to scale
Where panels meet (open corner)
Green: the standoff, 13 x 22 mm for a 4 mm screw, behind the corner tile's
centre slot (black outline, in front of it); its keyhole in white, the screw
in black. Grey dots: D237's standoff, built now. Red: the nearest point.
At a wall's outer corner (closed)
The same place on every panel: the screws on the slot grid,
20 mm in from each panel's side.
Behind the slot, the standoff keeps 11.25 mm clear of every other
slot and hook where panels meet, 9 mm from a closed edge; D237's
kept 1.28. Screws up to 6 mm fit, not only 4. The slot it stands
behind takes no hook, as IKEA's spacer takes its slot (D131):
two slots a board, both at the top.
a: the standoff closes the slot's back: from the front the board
looks like any other, that slot 5 mm deep.
b: the slot runs on through the standoff to the head's channel:
you see the screw head through the slot as you hang the board,
and a screwdriver through it tightens the screw, pulling the
standoff against the wall, as IKEA's spacer is screwed.
